question: Should this PR be narrowed to the Gateway consolidation before further merge review, or are maintainers intentionally accepting the unrelated bundled changes as one coordinated landing unit?
rationale: The observed 209-file merge surface conflicts with the PR’s stated narrow, behavior-preserving scope, and only an owner can confirm whether this is accidental branch contamination or an intentional combined landing.

options.title: Narrow to Gateway changes
options.body: Reconstruct or rebase the branch so it contains only the shared lifecycle, adapters, package wiring, and directly required tests.

options.title: Review as coordinated mega-change
options.body: Keep the combined branch and obtain explicit owner, dependency, generated-output, upgrade, and real-behavior evidence for every additional surface.

options.title: Pause the landing
options.body: Hold or replace the PR if a coherent focused head cannot be produced without discarding most unrelated changes.

recommendation.title: Narrow to Gateway changes
recommendation.body: Reconstruct or rebase the branch so it contains only the shared lifecycle, adapters, package wiring, and directly required tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows ownership of the gateway-client extraction and both existing client implementations, making this person the strongest available owner for the branch-scope choice.
